summary_en.motivation: To assess the potential of laser powder bed fusion for fabricating bionic porous titanium scaffolds for biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Porous Ti scaffolds were fabricated via LPBF, then characterized for compressive behavior, porosity, and surface roughness.
summary_en.result: The relationship between compressive properties and structural parameters was established, demonstrating feasibility.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical compression testing was used to validate the scaffold's performance.

papers.title: From shape to function—bioprinting technologies for tissue engineered grafts to meet clinical needs
papers.abstract: AbstractThe bottom-up approach of 3D bioprinting uses biopolymeric bioink along with the defined cells and allows to engineer 3D tissues/organs. The process is multistep, comprising upstream designing of matrix blueprints, bioinks, crosslinking strategies, and downstream maturation of construct using a bioreactor. The present review aims to provide a holistic picture of the various phases in 3D bioprinting, the methods used, and their clinical applications, such as in regenerative medicine, disease study, drug testing, and in situ bioprinting. Also, highlighted upgraded versions of 4D and 5D printing for better biomimetic properties and uses of 3D nanoprinting technology for effective tissue reconstruction.Keywords: Biomaterialsbiomimicry3D bioprinting3D nanoprintingscaffoldstissue engineering Ethical approvalThere are no animal experiments carried out for this article.Disclosure statementNo potential conflict of interest was reported by the author(s).Additional informationFundingThis study was supported by the Manipal School of Life Sciences, Manipal Academy of Higher Education. The authors would like to thank SERB, Government of India, for providing support through SRG funding (SRG/2021/001686).
